title: Senior UI/UX Designer – Medical Imaging Platform
description:
**About the Role**

We are building a cloud-native, AI-assisted radiology platform for CT and MRI, made up of a browser-based 3D viewer and the web application around it: worklists, study management, clinical workflows, administration, and an agentic AI assistant. The product is developed as a regulated medical device on the path to FDA 510(k) clearance.

We are looking for a UI/UX Designer with about five years of experience to own the design of this product end to end. You will design for radiologists and imaging staff who work for hours on dense, high-stakes images, and you will work side by side with our engineers, ML team, product, and QA to turn clinical needs into clear, safe, and efficient interfaces.

**Key Responsibilities**

**Product and Interaction Design**

* Own UX and UI design across the web application: worklists, search and filters, study and series management, case assignment, review and approval queues, reporting, and administration.
* Design the 3D viewer experience: layouts and hanging protocols, MPR and volume views, windowing and transfer function controls, measurements, annotations, and segmentation editing tools.
* Design for expert, high-volume use: keyboard shortcuts, mouse and touch interaction, low-latency feedback, and information-dense screens that stay readable.
* Map clinical workflows through research, then turn them into user flows, wireframes, interactive prototypes, and high-fidelity designs.

**AI-Assisted Workflow Design**

* Design how AI results (segmentations, findings, measurements) appear in the viewer and how clinicians review, edit, accept, or reject them.
* Design the interface for our agentic AI assistant: conversation, suggested actions, tool-use transparency, and clear confirmation steps before anything changes a case.
* Make AI output visibly distinct from clinician-entered content, and communicate confidence, provenance, and limitations without adding noise.

**Design System and Craft**

* Build and maintain a scalable design system in Figma: components, tokens, patterns, and documentation shared with the front-end team.
* Design dark-mode-first interfaces suited to reading rooms, with careful contrast, color use, and accessibility (WCAG 2.1 AA).
* Produce precise specs and review implemented UI with engineers to make sure the final product matches the design.

  

**Research, Validation, and Compliance**

* Plan and run usability studies with radiologists and technologists, from early concept tests to formative and summative evaluations.
* Support usability engineering for regulatory submissions (IEC 62366-1, FDA human factors guidance): use specifications, use-related risk analysis, and evaluation reports.
* Turn research findings and usage feedback into clear, prioritized design improvements.

**Required Qualifications**

* 5+ years of professional UI/UX or product design experience, with a portfolio showing complex, data-heavy web applications shipped to real users.
* Expert-level Figma: auto layout, variables and tokens, component libraries, and interactive prototyping.
* Proven experience building or evolving a design system used by engineering teams.
* Strong skills in user research and usability testing, and in turning findings into design decisions.
* Solid grasp of interaction design for expert tools: dense layouts, shortcuts, progressive disclosure, and error prevention.
* Working knowledge of accessibility standards (WCAG 2.1 AA), color contrast, and dark UI design.
* Good understanding of front-end constraints (HTML/CSS, React component thinking) to design buildable solutions and work closely with developers.
* Excellent written and verbal communication, and the ability to explain and defend design decisions to engineers, clinicians, and leadership.
* Preferred Qualifications
* Experience designing healthcare, medical imaging, PACS, or clinical software; familiarity with radiology workflows and viewer conventions.
* Experience designing AI or LLM-based products, including human-in-the-loop review and trust and transparency patterns.
* Familiarity with 3D, scientific, or visualization interfaces, such as CAD, GIS, or imaging tools.
* Exposure to regulated product design: IEC 62366-1, ISO 14971 risk concepts, FDA human factors, or similar.
* Skills in motion and micro-interaction design for feedback and state changes.
* Comfort prototyping with code (HTML/CSS, Storybook, or Tailwind) or with AI-assisted design tools.
* A Master's degree or specialization in HCI, interaction design, or a related field.

**What Success Looks Like in the First 6 Months**

* You understand our users' workflows through direct sessions with radiologists, and have documented the key flows and pain points.
* You have established the first version of our design system, adopted by the front-end team.
* You have designed and shipped at least one major workflow, such as the study worklist or AI result review, validated with real users.
* Your design documentation is traceable and ready to support usability engineering in regulatory submissions.

**What We Offer**

A chance to define the design language of an AI-enabled clinical imaging product used to improve patient care.

Real ownership and influence on product direction, working directly with engineering and clinical experts.

Direct access to radiologists and imaging specialists for research and feedback.

Competitive salary and benefits.

Flexible work arrangements and support for professional development.

You will establish a formal UX practice on the platform from the ground up and lead the designers and developers  

who join it. Strong stakeholder management and communication are central to the role. You will be the advocate for experience who aligns product, engineering, and business around a shared bar for quality, and holds us to it.


What you will do  

UX Standards and Consistency  

* Own and document the UX and UI standards for the platform, and drive their adoption across every team building on ServiceNow.
* Build and own a design system and component library so that consistency is built in, not policed after the fact.
* Establish design patterns, guidelines, and reusable components that raise the floor on every solution we ship.

Consumer Grade Experience and Adoption  

* Move the platform beyond a traditional ITSM mindset and design solutions where the experience is consumer grade.
* Own the success and adoption of the solutions we ship. Define what adoption looks like, measure it, and use


it to drive design decisions.  

* Partner with product and business teams to make sure we are solving the real user problem, not just delivering the requested feature.
* Bring an outside\-in view of quality, benchmarked against the consumer products our users actually compare us to.
  

  

Hands On Design and Build  

* Design and build experiences directly in UI Builder and the Now Experience Framework.
* Write front\-end code in React to build components, prototypes, and production experiences where native tooling is not enough.
* Move fluidly between design and implementation so that what gets shipped matches what was designed.

User Research and Accessibility

title: Delightree - Senior Design Engineer
description:
### **About the role**


This role splits roughly in half.


The first half is designing for franchise operations \- multi location brands, franchisee owners, and frontline staff each needing something different from the same product.


The second half is owning the layer between design and code. You'll own the design system \- the components, patterns, and code. You'll write frontend code yourself, and you'll define how design work becomes a shipped interface for everyone else on the team.


That second half is why this role exists. Our approach to product development is shifting. Instead of traditional mockup handoffs, product managers and designers directly build working prototypes directly in code, using AI workflows alongside our component library. Engineering builds on those prototypes rather than starting over. You own this system and ensure it's up to scale and quality.

### **What you'll do**

* Design and build UI in the same motion \- prototyping novel AI\-native interactions directly in code rather than in Figma\-then\-handoff, especially where no pattern library exists yet.
* Sit inside a pod (PM \+ eng lead \+ you) and take features from concept to shipped, rather than handing off a spec and waiting.
* Own the interaction and motion details \- loading/streaming states, transitions, micro\-interactions \- the polish that's nearly impossible to fully spec in a doc.
* Build and maintain shared UI components so the rest of the org can move fast without reinventing patterns feature by feature.
* Work directly in the production codebase.

### **What we're looking for**

* 4\+ years in product design, with depth in dense interfaces \- tables, forms, permissions, multi role flows.
* Real product/visual design judgment *and* the ability to ship real frontend code \- not a designer who dabbles in code or an engineer who cares about UI, but someone for whom design and implementation are the same skill.
* Hands\-on frontend engineering. A portfolio \+ GitHub showing shipped, interactive, polished products \- not just mockups or case studies.
* Design systems built and maintained at scale, in code. You should be able to direct AI tools to build and maintain prototypes that adhere to accessibility, component system, and other guardrails.
* Experience or strong interest in AI\-native interfaces: streaming output, agentic/human\-in\-the\-loop UX, confidence and uncertainty in UI.
* Bonus: has worked somewhere small enough that design and engineering weren't separate functions. AI used structurally in how features got shipped, from ideation through implementation and review \- not just for copy or asset generation.
